title: Order bindings by `id`. The `assignedmin` order is now ambiguous.
comment:
**Order bindings by `id`. The `assigned_min` order is now ambiguous.**

The docstring says the latest binding comes from `id` order. All readers still use only `order_by(TaskLinkBinding.assigned_min.desc())` and then fold with `setdefault`. The surrogate key now allows same-minute rebinding. When two rows tie on `assigned_min`, the database row order decides the "latest" binding.

Example: the seed binding `(T-A, L-1H, 0)` and a switch at scene minute 0, `(T-A, L-3H, 0)`, tie. `T-A` can still appear on `L-1H`. The consequences are wrong occupancy, wrong switch and restore candidates, and a wrong `task_carrier`.

Add `TaskLinkBinding.id.desc()` as a tiebreaker at each reader:
- `backend/app/services/occupancy.py` Lines 50-56 (`_load_link_tasks`)
- `backend/app/services/plan.py` Lines 32-38 and 77-83
- `backend/app/services/switch.py` Lines 25-31
- `backend/app/services/restore.py` Lines 46-52, 61-66, 74-80, and 203-209
- `backend/app/services/approval.py` Lines 403-409
- `backend/app/services/engine.py` Lines 564-568

```python
.order_by(TaskLinkBinding.assigned_min.desc(), TaskLinkBinding.id.desc())
```

title: Pass `asofmin` to `handlerepairupdate`.
comment:
**Pass `as_of_min` to `handle_repair_update`.**

The endpoint computes `est_abs` from `payload.as_of_min`. `handle_repair_update` does not receive that value, so it computes its own `now` from the clock. It then writes the `repair_received` event with `occur_min` set to the clock minute. The event minute and the stored finish minute therefore use different bases.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     result = handle_repair_update(
         db,
         order_code=payload.order_code,
         est_finish_min=est_abs,
         actual_finish_min=actual_abs,
+        as_of_min=payload.as_of_min,
     )
```
</details>

title: The booking producers in `comm.py` do not encode `task=`/`gbps=`, so their bookings insert the default `T-B`/`6.00`.
comment:
**The booking producers in `comm.py` do not encode `task=`/`gbps=`, so their bookings insert the default `T-B`/`6.00`.**

The parser reads `task=` and `gbps=` from `ev.summary`. Only the seed `EVT-0002` uses that format. `handle_input` in `backend/app/api/comm.py` (Lines 228-237) writes the summary as `"{minute_offset} 分钟后 {sub} -> {task_code}"`. A booked demand change for `T-A` at 8G therefore inserts a `T-B` demand at 6.00G. The `demand_added` alert reports the same wrong values. Check `_dispatch_parsed` in this file for the same format.

The `ref_code` value `D-{task}-BOOK` is fixed per task. If a task has two bookings, the second one returns early at Line 171.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed producer fix (backend/app/api/comm.py)</summary>

```diff
         else:
             ref_type = "demand"
-            ref_code = f"D-{params['task_code'][2:]}-BOOK"
+            ref_code = f"D-{params['task_code'][2:]}-BK{datetime.now().strftime('%H%M%S%f')}"
         ev = SceneEvent(
             ...
-            summary=(
-                f"{minute_offset} 分钟后 {sub} -> {params.get('link_code') or params.get('task_code')}"
-            ),
+            summary=(
+                f"task={params['task_code']};gbps={params['demand_gbps']};"
+                f"{minute_offset} 分钟后需求变更"
+                if ref_type == "demand"
+                else f"{minute_offset} 分钟后 {sub} -> {params.get('link_code')}"
+            ),
         )
```
</details>

title: The new holder check never fails, so `releasedlinks` stays empty.
comment:
**The new holder check never fails, so `released_links` stays empty.**

`holder_bindings` comes from a query filtered by `.where(TaskLinkBinding.link_code == holder)`. Every row therefore has `b.link_code == holder`. The first row sets `any_task = True`, so the behavior did not change. A holder is busy only when a task's global latest binding is on that holder.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
         seen: Set[str] = set()
         any_task: bool = False
         for b in holder_bindings:
             if b.task_code in seen:
                 continue
             seen.add(b.task_code)
-            if b.link_code == holder:
+            latest = db.scalar(
+                select(TaskLinkBinding)
+                .where(TaskLinkBinding.task_code == b.task_code)
+                .order_by(TaskLinkBinding.assigned_min.desc(), TaskLinkBinding.id.desc())
+                .limit(1)
+            )
+            if latest is not None and latest.link_code == holder:
                 any_task = True
                 break
```
</details>

`_current_load_on_link` (Lines 74-88) has the same problem. It also counts tasks that have moved away from the link.

title: The no-op path makes restore after an outage silently do nothing.
comment:
**The no-op path makes restore after an outage silently do nothing.**

`handle_link_down` sets the faulted link to `down`. `handle_link_restored` is the handler for the "线路1已恢复" input and for `POST /comm/links/{link_code}/restore`. Neither path sets the link back to `up`. Only `handle_repair_update` does that, and only with `actual_finish_min`. After a real outage, both restore entry points always reach this branch. They return an empty success result with `released_link_code` set, and no task moves back.

The restore request is the signal that the link is up again. On this path, set `link.oper_state = "up"`, write the `state_changed` event, and continue with candidate restoration.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     if link.oper_state != "up":
-        # 软处理：不抛错，写事件 + 推 toast + 返回空
+        prev = link.oper_state
+        link.oper_state = "up"
         db.add(
             SceneEvent(
                 event_code=f"EVT-RS-UP-{datetime.now().strftime('%H%M%S%f')}",
                 event_type="state_changed",
                 ref_type="link",
                 ref_code=link_code,
                 occur_min=now,
-                summary=f"{link_code} 状态为 {link.oper_state}，跳过回迁",
+                summary=f"{link_code} {prev} -> up（恢复通知）",
             )
         )
         db.flush()
-        ...
-        return {...}
```
</details>

title: The script crashes on the BOM in the first line of `crreview.ndjson`.
comment:
**The script crashes on the BOM in the first line of `cr_review.ndjson`.**

Line 1 of `cr_review.ndjson` starts with `\ufeff`. When the input begins with a BOM, `json.loads` raises `JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM`. On Windows, `sys.stdin` can also default to a non-UTF-8 code page, which corrupts the Chinese text. Read stdin as `utf-8-sig`.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-import sys, json
-lines = [json.loads(l) for l in sys.stdin if l.strip()]
+import io, sys, json
+stream = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdin.buffer, encoding="utf-8-sig")
+lines = [json.loads(l.lstrip("\ufeff")) for l in stream if l.strip()]
```
</details>

title: Map the `APV-{plancode}` codes from `createorgetapproval` back to plan codes.
comment:
**Map the `APV-{plan_code}` codes from `create_or_get_approval` back to plan codes.**

`create_or_get_approval` in `backend/app/api/comm.py` (Line 156) returns `APV-{plan_code}` to clients. Approval records use the key `APV-{plan_code}-{seq}`. For a legacy client that sends `approval_code=APV-PLAN-...`, `db.get(ApprovalRecord, target)` returns `None`. The code then sends `APV-PLAN-...` to `decide_approval` as a plan code, and the plan lookup fails.

If a record does exist, the plan already has a decision. `_do_decide` then rejects it because the status is not `待审批`. The legacy path therefore never succeeds.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     if payload.approval_code and not payload.plan_code:
         # 老路径：通过 approval_code 反查 plan_code
         ap: ApprovalRecord | None = db.get(ApprovalRecord, target)
         if ap is not None and ap.plan_code:
             target = ap.plan_code
+        elif target.startswith("APV-"):
+            # create_or_get_approval 返回的占位码 APV-{plan_code}
+            target = target[len("APV-"):]
```
</details>
